hubs.name: Appalachian Coal Country (Met & Thermal)
hubs.description: Metallurgical coal for steelmaking and thermal coal. CSX and NS built their networks around this corridor. Moves to Virginia/Baltimore ports for export or west to Midwest steel mills.

hubs.name: Baton Rouge (Gulf Petrochemical/Grain)
hubs.description: Southern terminus of the Mississippi River industrial corridor. Grain and chemicals transfer barge-to-ocean vessel. Connected to Gulf Intracoastal Waterway. CN, CSX, UP rail access.

hubs.name: BNSF Alliance Texas (Dallas Hub)
hubs.description: BNSF intermodal — ~600K container lifts annually, 16 double-stack trains daily. All-freight airport, FTZ, US Customs on site. UP also provides carload service to industrial tenants.

hubs.name: CenterPoint Joliet (Chicago Bypass Hub)
hubs.description: 6,500-acre inland port complex near Joliet, IL. BNSF and UP railheads. 10M+ sq ft of distribution space. Located on CN's EJ&E bypass route — freight avoids downtown Chicago congestion entirely.

hubs.name: Chicago (North America's Only Universal Interchange)
hubs.description: 25% of all US rail freight touches Chicago. Every Class I railroad converges here. Historically 24-36 hrs to hand off one car between carriers. CREATE Program modernizing infrastructure. CN's EJ&E bypass — Waukegan to Joliet ring — is the only completed Class I bypass in North America.

hubs.name: CPKC Jackson/Richland MS
hubs.description: One of 5 CPKC intermodal terminals in the US. Sits on former KCS mainline connecting Gulf of Mexico to Kansas City and Canada. Key node on the only single-railroad US-Canada-Mexico route.

hubs.name: Greer SC (BMW / Auto Parts Hub)
hubs.description: 175,873 containers moved in 2023 — up 26% year over year. Built specifically to serve BMW Spartanburg plant. NS rail connection to Port of Charleston. Auto parts inbound, finished vehicles outbound.

hubs.name: Gulf Coast Chemical Corridor
hubs.description: Largest petrochemical manufacturing corridor in the world — Houston Ship Channel to Baton Rouge. Tank cars and covered hoppers distribute chemicals and plastics to every corner of North America.

hubs.name: Jacksonville (JAXPORT, Forest Products Hub)
hubs.description: Major forest products import and export hub. Paper rolls from Finland and Sweden inbound. Pulp from Brazil. Southeast lumber and pulp outbound. CSX and NS connections. 240,000 sq ft on-dock covered warehouse.

hubs.name: Laredo TX (US/Mexico Rail Gateway via CPKC)
hubs.description: Primary US-Mexico rail crossing. CPKC's most strategic asset post-merger. Automotive parts, beer (Modelo/Corona), grain, manufactured goods, and steel coils cross daily. Gateway on the only single-railroad US-Canada-Mexico route in existence.

hubs.name: Los Angeles/Long Beach Cargo Terminal
hubs.description: Largest port complex in North America. Asian imports enter here and move east by UP and BNSF double-stack intermodal trains. Western gateway for all import container flows.

hubs.name: Louisville (Ohio River Rail/Barge Transfer)
hubs.description: Ohio River transfer point. 23,000-ft double-loop rail track receives full 120-car unit trains. Entire train off-loaded in one 8-hour shift directly into barges. Primary commodities: coal, grain, fertilizer, potash.

hubs.name: Memphis (Multi-Modal Crossroads)
hubs.description: 5th largest inland port in the US. Mississippi River barge access + 5 Class I railroads + interstate highway convergence + FedEx air hub. Every freight mode touches Memphis.

hubs.name: Midwest Corn Belt (Grain / Steel / Autos)
hubs.description: Center of gravity for US grain — corn and soybeans move to Gulf export elevators or east to ports. Steel from Indiana mills feeds auto plants. Every Class I railroad converges on Chicago.

hubs.name: Northern Plains (Grain / Bakken Crude)
hubs.description: Wheat, corn, canola, and Bakken crude oil. One of the most freight-dense rail corridors in North America. BNSF dominant.

hubs.name: Port of Baltimore (Autos & Farm Equipment)
hubs.description: #1 US port for autos, farm and construction machinery, imported forest products, sugar, and aluminum. CSX and NS Class I connections. Seagirt Marine Terminal and Dundalk — 570 acres of cargo handling.

hubs.name: Port of Houston (National Leader)
hubs.description: National leader in break bulk cargo volume. Dominates oil and gas equipment, steel pipe, wind turbine components, heavy lift project cargo. All Class I rail carriers accessible via Ship Channel.

hubs.name: Port of Mobile (#1 US Forest Products)
hubs.description: Largest break bulk forest products port in the United States. Dockside rail facility — direct car-to-vessel transfer. CN is primary rail carrier from the Southeast pine belt. Also serves steel and chemicals. Website: alports.com

hubs.name: Port of New Orleans
hubs.description: 97 miles inland on the Mississippi River — unique convergence of river barge, rail, and ocean vessel. All 6 Class I railroads serve this port. Iron and steel imports, chemicals, project cargo, grain export.

hubs.name: Port of NY/NJ Cargo Terminal
hubs.description: Third-busiest US port by volume. Enormous inbound container flows move inland by rail and truck. Scrap metal moves outbound to Midwest mills. CSX and NS serve the region.

hubs.name: Port of Virginia (Offshore Wind Surge)
hubs.description: 372% surge in break bulk driven by offshore wind — tower sections, nacelles, turbine blades. CSX and NS connections. Fastest growing break bulk segment in the US driven by the energy buildout.

hubs.name: Powder River Basin (Coal)
hubs.description: Largest coal-producing region in North America. BNSF and UP run dedicated unit trains east to Midwest power plants and west to Pacific Coast export terminals.

hubs.name: Saskatchewan Potash Mines
hubs.description: World's largest potash reserves. CP/CPKC's most important single commodity. Moves south by rail to US fertilizer markets.

hubs.name: Savannah Garden City Terminal (SE Intermodal Gateway)
hubs.description: 3rd largest container port in the US and fastest growing. Foreign auto plants — BMW, Mercedes, Hyundai — generate massive rail car flows. CSX and NS connections. Expanding capacity through 2040.

hubs.name: Seattle/Tacoma Cargo Terminal (Pacific Northwest)
hubs.description: Northwest Seaport Alliance — break bulk, containers, project cargo, autos. Forest products moving outbound from Pacific Northwest timber country. BNSF and UP connections. Canadian and US grain export via Vancouver.

hubs.name: Southeast Pine Belt (Forest Products)
hubs.description: MS, AL, GA, SC pine belt produces wood pulp, cellulose rolls, kraft liner board, and lumber. CN (former Illinois Central) and CSX/NS move product to Gulf and Atlantic break bulk terminals.

hubs.name: St. Louis (Primary River Transfer Point)
hubs.description: 15 barge transfer facilities — highest handling capacity anywhere on the Mississippi River. Connected to BNSF, CN, CSX, NS, and UP. 32M+ tons/year. Grain arrives by rail from the Corn Belt, loads onto barges, moves south to Gulf export terminals.

hubs.name: Vancouver BC (Canadian Grain & Potash Export)
hubs.description: Western terminus for Canadian and US Prairie grain exports to Asia. CN and CP compete for this corridor. State-of-the-art grain handling. Pacific gateway for North American agricultural and potash exports.

hubs.name: Vancouver BC (US/Canada Rail Gateway)
hubs.description: CN and CP primary US-Canada crossing point. Canadian grain, potash, and forest products move south. Import containers move north. Western gateway for trans-Pacific trade flows in both directions.

hubs.name: Kansas City Rail Hub (Universal Interchange #2)
hubs.description: Second-largest rail interchange in North America after Chicago. Six Class I railroads meet here — BNSF, UP, NS, CSX, CPKC, plus KCT terminal switching. Major intermodal yards: BNSF Argentine (Kansas side), KCS/CPKC Knoche Yard, NS Voltz Yard. Primary East-West and North-South pivot for grain, autos, and intermodal.

hubs.name: North Platte (UP Bailey Yard — World's Largest)
hubs.description: World's largest rail classification yard — 2,850 acres, 315 miles of track, ~14,000 cars handled per day. Hump yard with 8 retarder tracks. Critical pivot for Powder River Basin coal trains heading east, intermodal lanes, and grain. Operated by Union Pacific.

hubs.name: Omaha (UP HQ / Bakken Grain Yard)
hubs.description: Union Pacific corporate headquarters. Major grain and Bakken-related yard activity. UP Council Bluffs Yard sits across the Missouri River and handles classification for the central corridor. Gateway between Midwestern grain belt and the Western network.

hubs.name: Council Bluffs (UP Yard)
hubs.description: UP yard complex paired with Omaha across the Missouri River. Critical for grain, ethanol, and intermodal interchange between the Midwest and Western networks.

hubs.name: Pueblo (EVRAZ Rocky Mountain Steel)
hubs.description: EVRAZ Rocky Mountain Steel — the only rail manufacturer west of the Mississippi (formerly CF&I). Produces long rail, seamless tube, and rebar. Both BNSF and UP serve the plant. Primary commodity origin for rebar and rail moving across the western US.

hubs.name: Denver (UP/BNSF Front Range Hub)
hubs.description: Front Range rail hub — UP's North Yard and BNSF's 36th Street Yard. Primary interchange for intermodal moving the Powder River-to-California and Texas-to-Pacific Northwest corridors. Key pivot for cement, building materials, and intermodal serving the Mountain West.

hubs.name: Wichita (Grain & Aerospace)
hubs.description: Hard red winter wheat country — major grain elevator concentration. Spirit AeroSystems and Textron (Cessna/Beechcraft) generate significant rail traffic for aerospace materials inbound. BNSF and UP both serve the city.

hubs.name: Topeka (BNSF Hub)
hubs.description: BNSF mid-Kansas yard on the transcon. Goodyear and Frito-Lay generate carload traffic. Pivot point between Kansas City and the western grain country.

hubs.name: Belen / Albuquerque (BNSF Transcon)
hubs.description: Belen Yard is BNSF's primary classification yard on the Transcon between Los Angeles and Chicago. Handles intermodal and merchandise traffic. Albuquerque sits 30 miles north on the same line. Critical western chokepoint for the Asian-import-to-Midwest container flow.

hubs.name: Sioux Falls (Northern Plains Grain)
hubs.description: Eastern South Dakota grain country — corn and soybean terminals serve BNSF and CPKC (former DM&E and IC&E lines). Ethanol-related shuttle loading. Gateway between the corn belt and Northern Plains wheat country.

hubs.name: Salt Lake City (UP Intermodal)
hubs.description: UP intermodal terminal serving the Mountain West. UP Roper Yard handles classification. Pivot between Pacific Northwest, California, and the Midwest. Primary route for Wasatch Front industrial outbound.

hubs.name: Duluth-Superior (Great Lakes Port — Iron Ore & Grain)
hubs.description: Largest port on the Great Lakes by tonnage. Primary Great Lakes export point for Mesabi Range taconite (iron ore pellets) and Northern Plains grain. BNSF, CN, and CPKC all reach the docks. Lake vessels move taconite to Lower Lakes steel mills (Gary, Cleveland, Detroit).

hubs.name: Mesabi Range (US Iron Ore Origin)
hubs.description: US iron ore origin — Cleveland-Cliffs and US Steel taconite operations (Hibbing, Minntac, United Taconite, Northshore). Pellets move by rail to Duluth-Superior or Two Harbors for Lake vessel export to Lower Lakes steel mills. BNSF and CN both serve the range.

hubs.name: Twin Cities (Minneapolis-St. Paul Grain Hub)
hubs.description: Historic grain milling center (Cargill, General Mills, ADM headquarters region). BNSF Northtown Yard is the largest classification yard in the Upper Midwest. CPKC, UP, and CN all interchange here. Mississippi headwaters barge access plus rail-to-Duluth or rail-to-Chicago routing.

hubs.name: Detroit / Dearborn (Auto Manufacturing Hub)
hubs.description: Center of US auto manufacturing — Ford (Dearborn), GM (Detroit-Hamtramck), Stellantis (Detroit and surrounding plants). All major Class I railroads reach the metro. Inbound: steel coils, parts, plastics. Outbound: finished vehicles to ports and dealers nationwide. CN's Flat Rock auto facility is a primary outbound multi-level loading point.

hubs.name: Toledo (Lake Erie Coal & Iron Ore Port)
hubs.description: Largest US port on Lake Erie. Coal export terminal for thermal and metallurgical coal moving by rail from Appalachia. Iron ore inbound from Lake vessels for Cleveland-Cliffs Toledo HBI plant and regional steel. CSX and NS direct rail access to dock facilities.

hubs.name: Cleveland (Cleveland-Cliffs Steel Hub)
hubs.description: Cleveland-Cliffs Cleveland Works — flat-rolled integrated steel mill. Lake Erie iron ore inbound, finished coils outbound to auto plants. CSX and NS both serve the mill. Major outbound steel coil flows to Detroit, Indianapolis, and the South.

hubs.name: Gary / Hammond (US Steel & Cleveland-Cliffs)
hubs.nearest_class_i: BNSF, UP, NS, CSX, CN, CPKC
hubs.description: Largest concentration of integrated steel-making capacity in the US. US Steel Gary Works, Cleveland-Cliffs Indiana Harbor (East Chicago), ArcelorMittal Burns Harbor nearby. All Class I railroads reach the district via Indiana Harbor Belt and EJ&E. Iron ore from Lake vessels in, steel coils out.

hubs.name: Indianapolis (CSX/NS Crossroads)
hubs.description: CSX Avon Yard and NS Hawthorne Yard. Major Midwest auto-parts and intermodal interchange. Pivot for Great Lakes-to-Southeast lanes. Auto plants in Indianapolis, Lafayette (Subaru), and Greensburg (Honda) generate inbound parts traffic.

hubs.name: Cincinnati (CSX Queensgate Hub)
hubs.description: CSX Queensgate Yard — major classification yard for the Midwest-Southeast and Midwest-Mid-Atlantic corridors. NS also serves the city. Ohio River barge interchange. Procter & Gamble and major auto-parts shippers generate carload traffic.

hubs.name: Milwaukee (Grain & Beverage Hub)
hubs.description: CPKC headquarters operations (legacy CP). Major grain milling and beverage industry (Miller-Coors). Lake Michigan port for limited Great Lakes vessel traffic. CPKC, CN, and UP all serve the metro.

hubs.name: Pine Bluff (UP Yard)
hubs.description: UP's primary classification yard between Little Rock and Texarkana. Forest products (paper mills) and chemicals dominate carload traffic. Gateway between Memphis-area interchange and the Houston/Mexico corridors.

hubs.name: Spokane (PNW Grain Corridor)
hubs.description: Inland Pacific Northwest hub on BNSF's Northern Transcon. Wheat country (Palouse) origin. BNSF Yardley Yard handles classification. Primary feed point for grain shuttle trains heading west to Seattle/Portland export terminals.

hubs.name: Birmingham (Southern Steel Belt)
hubs.description: Historic Southern steel center — Nucor Steel Birmingham, CMC Steel Alabama, US Pipe. Mini-mill EAF capacity producing rebar and structural steel. All major Class I railroads reach the district. Outbound coil and bar moves nationwide.

hubs.name: Pittsburgh (Steel & Coal Origin)
hubs.description: Historic US steel capital — US Steel Mon Valley Works (Edgar Thomson, Irvin, Clairton coke). Cleveland-Cliffs Butler Works nearby. Met coal from southwestern PA moves out by rail. NS and CSX both serve the Mon Valley. Ohio River barge interchange at confluence.

hubs.name: Roseville (UP Yard for SF Bay Area)
hubs.description: UP J.R. Davis Yard — largest classification yard in the western US. Primary intermodal and merchandise pivot for Northern California, including the SF Bay Area, Sacramento Valley agriculture, and the Donner Pass crossing of the Sierra Nevada.

hubs.name: Phoenix / Tucson (Mexico-LA Corridor)
hubs.description: Sun Belt distribution hub — BNSF and UP both reach the Phoenix metro. Tucson sits on UP's Sunset Route between Los Angeles and El Paso/Mexico. Massive growth in semiconductor (TSMC), data center, and EV battery inbound traffic.

hubs.name: Jacksonville (CSX Headquarters Rail Hub)
hubs.description: CSX corporate headquarters and CSX Jacksonville Intermodal Terminal. Distinct from JAXPORT (already on map as forest-products port). Primary Southeast classification node for CSX — the I-95 corridor from New England to Florida pivots here.

hubs.name: Selkirk (CSX New York Hub)
hubs.description: CSX Selkirk Yard — primary classification yard for CSX in upstate New York. Major pivot for New England traffic and the Albany-area auto-parts and consumer-goods flow. NS interchange with Pan Am Southern.

hubs.name: Tulsa (BNSF / UP Crude & Grain)
hubs.description: Cushing crude oil hub sits 60 miles southwest — pipeline-rail interface for the WTI benchmark. BNSF Cherokee Yard and UP yards serve refining and petrochemical-adjacent traffic. Wheat outbound from Oklahoma elevators.

hubs.name: St. Paul (BNSF Northtown Annex)
hubs.description: Sister yard to Twin Cities/Minneapolis. CPKC's primary Twin Cities classification activity, plus UP and CN connections. Mississippi River barge head-of-navigation.

hubs.name: Fort Worth (BNSF HQ)
hubs.description: BNSF corporate headquarters. Distinct from BNSF Alliance (already on map) — Fort Worth proper hosts BNSF's operating HQ and a network of yards including Hodge and Tower 55, the busiest rail diamond in the US where BNSF and UP cross.

hubs.name: East St. Louis (BNSF / NS / CSX)
hubs.nearest_class_i: BNSF, NS, CSX, UP, CN, CPKC
hubs.description: East-side complement to St. Louis barge hub already on map. All six Class I railroads reach the East St. Louis terminal area via Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis (TRRA). Major auto and intermodal flows.

hubs.name: Nashville (CSX Radnor Yard)
hubs.description: CSX Radnor Yard — Tennessee classification hub. GM Spring Hill and Nissan Smyrna plants generate auto-parts inbound and finished-vehicle outbound traffic. Pivot for Southeast-to-Midwest corridors.

hubs.name: Atlanta (NS Inman / CSX Hulsey)
hubs.description: NS Inman Yard and CSX Hulsey Yard. Largest Southeast metro intermodal market. KIA West Point and Hyundai Metaplant Georgia inbound parts. Container flows from Savannah inland.

hubs.name: El Paso / Santa Teresa (UP / BNSF Mexico Gateway)
hubs.description: Secondary US-Mexico rail crossing — UP Sunset Route and the Santa Teresa NM intermodal facility (BNSF). Complement to Laredo (CPKC). Auto parts, electronics, and produce cross daily. Foxconn and EV battery investment driving growth.

hubs.name: Toronto (CN MacMillan / CPKC Toronto Yard)
hubs.description: CN MacMillan Yard (one of the largest in North America) and CPKC Toronto Yard. Primary Canadian eastern hub. Auto manufacturing (Ford Oakville, Stellantis Brampton, Toyota Cambridge nearby) generates rail flows. Gateway for Canadian Pacific to US Midwest via Buffalo/Detroit.
